quarterly_data.quarter: Vicor press release: Vicor Corporation Raises Q3 2026 Revenue Guidance (09-21-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: On September 21, 2026 Vicor raised its Q3 2026 sequential revenue growth guidance from nearly 10% to more than 20%, in view of royalties from a recently announced non-exclusive license to Vertical Power Delivery (VPD). The licensee is not named in the release and no dollar figure is given.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 sequential growth guidance raised from nearly 10% to more than 20%

quarterly_data.quarter: Vicor press release: Vicor Corporation Raises Q3 2026 Revenue Guidance (09-21-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: IP licensing (CEO Patrizio Vinciarelli, in the release): among OEMs and hyperscalers, four leading companies have secured licenses to power system technology pioneered and patented by Vicor. Unlicensed hyperscalers first reached out after their computing systems were banned from importation because of infringing NBMs, and on recognizing that computing systems using VPD could also be banned. Because the first VPD patent was only recently asserted, a license can still be secured at an early stage of escalation with a low royalty rate. He adds that suppliers selling otherwise infringing power modules to licensed OEMs and hyperscalers contribute to multi-source supply chains, while suppliers that disregard Vicor's patents 'will continue to cause supply disruption to their customers and be liable for monetary damages to Vicor' and may be excluded from supplying power systems covered by Vicor patents. Licensees are not named.
quarterly_data.figure: four leading companies (OEMs and hyperscalers) licensed; first VPD patent only recently asserted
